findings.title: Incomplete token-matching records can still admit inherited diagnostics

locations.reason: The per-stream pending tail is never validated on stream end or child close.
A line containing the exact marker and token but no trailing space/payload is silently treated as unrelated output.
A previously valid completed record leaves done=true because neither ignored case sets invalid.

findings.source_explanation: After a valid BEGIN and END, a duplicate END or malformed END without a final newline stays in pending and is discarded. Even with a newline, QA_ADMITTED_COMMAND <exact-token> without the expected final space fails the prefix check and is discarded. In all three cases completed remains set and invalid remains false. A nonzero Task result and matching TypeScript diagnostic then enter the inherited-diagnostic comparison as a completed run.
findings.impact: Violates the explicit acceptance rule that malformed, duplicate or inconsistent completion evidence must never classify a run as inherited diagnostics. This is a protocol fault-injection result, not a claim that the unmodified host reporter normally emits these malformed records.

findings.requested_correction: Validate token-matching incomplete records and stream tails before accepting completion, including records missing the event separator. Preserve rejection of duplicate records and all existing timeout, signal and status checks. Add focused regression coverage for these three demonstrated cases. The manager owns the correction.

source_only_conclusions.conclusion: Sorted retained spans charge their union. Concurrent branch runs share one budget object; sequential main comparisons share a distinct single object. Each admitted compiler contributes a span, while the parent timer remains authoritative even if a child received an older remaining-budget snapshot.

The gate computes qaMemoryDeadline once, preserves the inherited deadline or defaults to six hours from entry, and propagates it into Task admission. Admission is independently finite and stops charging its timer once that compiler has begun.

Actual Task typecheck entries continue through the host CPU/memory wrapper. The outer flock relay retains protocol controls; final admission consumes the token, descriptor and command budget before starting compiler descendants. CPU permits release in finally.

For recognized full records, the parser checks BEGIN/END order, timestamps, numeric status range, duplicate events, timeout/signal indicators and Task success/failure consistency. Task maps inner nonzero exits to status 201, so success/failure equivalence is intentional. These checks do not cover the incomplete-record finding.

END starts the separate 5000ms Task/permit-shutdown bound and closes the compiler span. A timeout awaits stopProcessGroup; the host wrapper also awaits any initiated termination before reporting END. The existing process helper snapshots descendant groups, signals them, freezes/kills survivors and uses bounded post-kill waits.

Only the exact known old host-admission blob enables the legacy exception. Its explicitly logged shared wall budget begins at main-budget creation before baseline checkout/install and is not reset between comparisons. Unknown/partial sources get the ordinary protocol path; a missing blob lookup throws and cannot enable legacy mode. Acceptance on the ordinary protocol path remains subject to the blocking parser finding.

CPU fixtures name private SQLite state and private slot directories; the gate fixture also gives its CPU override a private directory and lock. Injected readers/clocks keep fixture pressure independent of live Goal admission limits; no policy or fixture budget was raised.
